title: Find Minimum Time to Reach Last Room II
summary: In a grid of n x m rooms, you start at (0,0) at time 0.
statement: In a grid of n x m rooms, you start at (0,0) at time 0. Each room has a moveTime indicating the earliest start time. You move to adjacent rooms, alternating between one and two seconds per move. Find the minimum time to reach (n-1,m-1).
constraints: move_time is a 2–750 by 2–750 nonnegative matrix.
Starting at (0,0), move durations alternate 1,2,1,2,... while entry may wait for the destination opening time.
Return the earliest arrival at the bottom-right room using four-directional moves.
hints: Grid bipartiteness fixes move-count parity from (row+col), even when a route detours.
Use Dijkstra and derive the next duration as (row+col)%2+1 at the current room.
Wait for the neighbor to open, add the parity-derived duration, and relax its arrival.
Every route to one cell has the same step parity, so one best-time label per cell is sufficient and Dijkstra remains valid.
editorial: Every route to one cell has the same step parity, so one best-time label per cell is sufficient and Dijkstra remains valid.

tests.explanation: After waiting to time four, moves of one and two seconds arrive at time seven.
Four moves cost 1+2+1+2, so the empty-opening grid takes six seconds.
